sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: The verb form usually shows who is doing the action, so Hungarian often leaves the subject pronoun unstated.

Nézek already means 'I watch' — tacking Én in front (Én nézek) isn't wrong, but it's like saying 'I, I watch'; the ending has already told you who. A named subject like Anna, though, has to be stated — the verb form alone can't tell you it's her and not you.
